title.en: Terminal molecular axial flux and velocity
title.zh: 终态分子轴向通量与流速归约

summary: Reduce a terminal H2 distribution to axial flux and mean velocity using an explicitly supplied thermal speed and radial/axial quadrature. This narrow variant accepts zero-weight cells with positive integrated density and does not compute higher moments.

capability: Terminal molecular axial flux and velocity

Reduce a terminal H2 distribution to axial flux and mean velocity using an explicitly supplied thermal speed and radial/axial quadrature. This narrow variant accepts zero-weight cells with positive integrated density and does not compute higher moments.
operation: reduce terminal axial flux and mean velocity
terminal (vr,vx,x) distribution, normalized axial nodes, explicit thermal speed and quadrature -> two x profiles
discovery.model: terminal H2 diagnostic with a caller-supplied thermal speed
discovery.geometry: one-dimensional x profile over a cylindrical (vr,vx) velocity carrier; radial nodes themselves are not required
discovery.boundary: finite, nonnegative nonempty three-dimensional distribution; finite one-dimensional vx, radial weights and axial widths with aligned sizes; radial weights and widths may be zero; finite positive thermal speed and strictly positive integrated density per x cell

identity.relation: terminal H2 axial flux and mean-velocity reduction
identity.direction: terminal (vr,vx,x) distribution, normalized axial nodes, explicit thermal speed and quadrature -> two x profiles
identity.definition: For each spatial cell k, density[k]=sum_i cylindrical_weight[i]*sum_j terminal_distribution[i,j,k]*dvx[j]; flux[k]=thermal_speed_m_s*sum_i cylindrical_weight[i]*sum_j vx[j]*terminal_distribution[i,j,k]*dvx[j], using the source's per-cell matrix-vector and radial summation order. mean_velocity[k]=flux[k]/density[k]. Density must be strictly positive although individual quadrature cells may have zero weight.
identity.model: terminal H2 diagnostic with a caller-supplied thermal speed
identity.geometry: one-dimensional x profile over a cylindrical (vr,vx) velocity carrier; radial nodes themselves are not required
identity.coordinates: vx is normalized by the supplied thermal speed; flux and mean velocity use that speed without implicit conversion
identity.boundary: finite, nonnegative nonempty three-dimensional distribution; finite one-dimensional vx, radial weights and axial widths with aligned sizes; radial weights and widths may be zero; finite positive thermal speed and strictly positive integrated density per x cell
assumptions: On positive quadrature weights this flux and velocity relation agrees with the corresponding fields of scirel.kinetic.axisymmetric-neutral-moments when that asset's derived thermal speed equals this caller-supplied speed. It remains a separate input/failure contract: the nine-moment asset requires vr, temperature, mass, strictly positive volume weights and higher-moment evaluation.
This callable does not infer a terminal generation, advance state, validate the producer of the incoming distribution or claim a full terminal closure.
The source's float coercion of boolean or numeric-string inputs is not part of this maintained real-numeric contract.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.description: Normalized axial velocity nodes; zero-valued nodes are valid.
inputs.constraints: Finite and one-dimensional with at least one node; no monotonicity or nonzero-node gate is imposed.

inputs.name: thermal_speed_m_s
inputs.description: Caller-supplied H2 thermal speed used by the axial-flux integral.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; boolean and numeric-string coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: terminal_distribution
inputs.description: Terminal H2 velocity distribution by spatial cell.
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative and nonempty with exactly three axes.

inputs.name: cylindrical_weight
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative and one-dimensional; zero cells are allowed if every integrated density stays positive.

inputs.name: dvx
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative and one-dimensional; zero cells are allowed if every integrated density stays positive.

outputs.name: flux_profile_m2_s
outputs.description: Signed terminal H2 axial particle-flux profile.
outputs.constraints: Finite; signed values follow the signed axial nodes.

outputs.name: mean_velocity_profile_m_s
outputs.description: Terminal H2 mean axial flow velocity.
outputs.constraints: Finite; equals flux divided by positive integrated density.

preconditions: The caller supplies a terminal H2 distribution aligned to the explicit velocity quadrature.
Every spatial slice has strictly positive integrated density.
supported: Stateless axial flux and velocity reduction on finite cylindrical terminal carriers, including some zero quadrature cells.
excluded: Higher pressure/stress/heat moments, generation-state selection, wall-source feedback and external physical validation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric or non-finite inputs, malformed axes, negative distribution/weights/widths, nonpositive thermal speed or a nonpositive integrated density.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if density, flux or mean velocity becomes non-finite; no partial mapping is returned.

example.description: Reduce one terminal H2 cell with a zero axial node and a zero-width cell.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import reduce_terminal_molecular_flux_velocity
vx = np.array([-1., 0., 2.])
f = np.ones((2, 3, 1))
r = reduce_terminal_molecular_flux_velocity(vx, 5000., f, np.array([1., 2.]), np.array([0.5, 0., 0.25]))
assert set(r) == {'flux_profile_m2_s', 'mean_velocity_profile_m_s'}
assert r['flux_profile_m2_s'].shape == (1,)
assert all(np.isfinite(value).all() for value in r.values())
example.expected: Two finite one-cell profiles; zero velocity nodes and zero-width cells are accepted when integrated density remains positive.

scope: Independent per-cell reduction checks both outputs on a nonuniform signed carrier.
Positive-weight overlap agrees with the existing nine-moment relation; zero-weight acceptance distinguishes their contracts.
Three digest-pinned fixed cases cover exact finite agreement and the boolean-coercion divergence.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct numerical comparisons establish the stated finite discrete relation and boundary differences on tested carriers. They do not establish the incoming terminal distribution, physical normalization, complete qualification or expert approval.
known_limitations: Numerical agreement with the reference cases is bounded evidence and does not establish full qualification.
The physical normalization of the supplied distribution and source flux label requires expert review.
